svg.title: The Universe of Bytes as a torus — the frequency circle, the amplitude circle, and the donut hole
svg.desc: A topological figure, dark theme. On the left, a torus drawn in perspective. Its hole is empty and carries the empty-set symbol: when the byte sequence is the empty set we are in the donut hole, which is the zero point, genesis, and is NOT a point of the torus surface — the hole is where the axis of revolution passes. Two small boxes above the torus declare the type "an empty byte sequence" and the type "a zero-number test", joined by the aspect "is detected by". Around the top of the tube a dashed cyan circle is marked THE FREQUENCY CIRCLE: position in the walk, the ring buffer Z/N, along which PREVIOUS and NEXT move. Standing across the tube on the right a purple circle is marked THE AMPLITUDE CIRCLE: the byte value, Z/256, which wraps so that NEXT at 255 is 0. A short purple arrow on that circle is labelled delta, the displacement. On the right, the same torus is drawn unrolled as the FUNDAMENTAL SQUARE — a rectangle whose top and bottom edges are identified, marked with matching single purple arrowheads, and whose left and right edges are identified, marked with matching double cyan arrowheads. The horizontal axis is FREQUENCY, the sequence of bytes being walked; the vertical axis is AMPLITUDE, the byte at that position, from 0 at the bottom to 255 at the top. Three green dots plot the word cat as the bytes 0x63, 0x61, 0x74, that is 99, 97 and 116. A solid green arrow from the first dot to the second is labelled delta equals minus 2. A second green arrow to the third dot is labelled delta equals plus 19. A dashed purple route leaves the first dot going up, exits through the top edge at 255, re-enters through the bottom edge at 0, and arrives at the same second dot: it is labelled plus 254, showing that minus 2 and plus 254 are the same move on a circle. Below, two olog regions. The left region is a LAYOUT, a finite limit: the type "a point of the universe of bytes" reaches "a position on the frequency circle" and "a byte value" both directly and through "a pair of a position and a byte value"; the two triangles commute, and that commuting is what the word product means. The right region is a FACT, a commuting square: "an ordered byte pair" reaches "a byte value" either directly, by its second component, or by demodulating to "a byte value with a displacement" and modulating back. That square is the statement that you GO THERE by displacement rather than looking a value up. At the foot, three panels state the law, the exact status of every claim asserted versus merely illustrated, and what the diagram cannot show.

arrow.label: is left by one genesis fold

commutes.reason: THE TORUS CLAIM, first projection. Asserts that a point of the universe of bytes IS the pair (position, byte) — i.e. that the total space of cat-byte.rzk (fiber = byte values 0..255 over base C = Z/N, the ring buffer) is the PRODUCT of the frequency circle and the amplitude circle, so that reading the position directly equals taking the pair and keeping the first. HELD 2026-08-24: this is READING A of foundation.md Q1, which is OPEN — Foundation says a ruling is owed BEFORE anything is drawn on it. AND the two obligations this reason used to name are ALREADY DISCHARGED in the corpus, so it was also under-claiming: Z/256 cyclic is FORCED (foundation.md 4.2), and the bundle is TRIVIAL because A-fiber is CONSTANT, position-independent (cat-bytes.md 3d). CITED, not redrawn.

THE TORUS CLAIM, second projection. Same status as c-torus-pi1: the VALUE factor Z/256 is FORCED (foundation.md 4.2) and cited, but naming the OTHER factor the ring buffer is READING A of the open Q1. Together the two projections are the T2 statement, which foundation.md 4.1 already asserts and says MUST NOT BE REDRAWN.

CITED, NOT NEW — cat-bytes.md 0.1 already asserts this in its own words (Frame-walk, not lookup; a lookup table has no from genealogy and no walk). GO THERE, DO NOT LOOK UP. For an ordered byte pair (a,b): reading b directly equals demodulating to the displacement d = b - a and modulating back, a + d = b. This is CarrierKernel's Modulate/Demodulate at the byte tier, and it is what makes steele's 'we simply GO THERE' a MOVE rather than a lookup. It reduces to group arithmetic in Z/256, but no #def is cited, so the obligation is left OPEN. THIS ONE IS GENUINELY NEW: neither cat-bytes.md nor foundation.md draws the fundamental square or this convergence, and it rides only on the VALUE circle, which is FORCED on either reading of Q1.

THE WRAP. Stepping by -2 and stepping by +254 are the SAME MOVE, because -2 = 254 in Z/256. Drawn statically as two routes leaving the o point (0x6f) and arriving at the m point (0x6d), one direct and one through the seam; the ANIMATION sends a head down each and they arrive TOGETHER, which is what makes this an assertion rather than a caption. It reduces to arithmetic in Z/256, but no #def is cited, so the obligation is left OPEN rather than claimed PROVEN off a peer-accepted appeal. NOTE the modelling decision: both routes also advance ONE position on the frequency circle, so these are arrows on a POINT of the universe, not on the byte factor alone; that position step is Q1-dependent while the displacement is not.

asserts.how: two heads leave the c point together, one by -2 and one by +254 through the amplitude seam, and ARRIVE TOGETHER at the a point. The convergence IS the claim.
the head leaves the hole and lands on the surface. The ARROW is asserted; see below for what the drawn trajectory is not.

illustrates.what: the swept CURVE of the genesis glide
illustrates.why: the genesis fold is ONE step. The path the head sweeps from the hole to the surface is not a morphism and its intermediate points are not states.
the frequency circle is Z/N and DISCRETE. Continuous motion between position 0 and position 1 does NOT assert that anything lies between them; it is the eye being carried, not a path being claimed.

illustrates.what: one full turn back to position 0
illustrates.why: illustrates the cyclic successor of the base. N is NOT ruled by this diagram, so the number of positions in the turn is a drawing choice.

illustrates.what: where each byte sits on the tube
illustrates.why: the meridian origin is the same DRAWING CONVENTION the caveat panel already declares. Nothing fixes it.

CHART-DEPENDENT, and I ran the control rather than assert it. What SURVIVES a chart change: the space is the MINIMUM byte in both ascii (0x20) and cp037 (0x40), so the dips are real under both. What FAILS: the two DEEPEST STEPS are the word boundaries in ascii (-69, -78) but NOT in cp037, where M-to-a (-83), inside a word, beats e-to-space (-69). So the dips are drawn and the deepest-step reading is NOT claimed.

illustrates.what: the three amplitude BANDS (space / upper / lower)
illustrates.why: a fact about the ascii chart, not about walks. Measured: ascii puts lower ABOVE upper (97-116 vs 67-77); cp037 INVERTS it (129-163 vs 195-212). Same word, same walk, different geometry — which is foundation.md 4b.2's iota-versus-tau leg distinction showing up as visible shape.

illustrates.what: drawing only the first WORD on the perspective torus
illustrates.why: not an editorial cut but a measured limit of the PROJECTION: at 38 degrees the band visible at EVERY longitude is psi 54..126, i.e. 72 of 360 degrees = 51 byte values = 20 percent of the amplitude circle. Composable spans 48 and fits with zero occlusion; the full string spans 84 and does not. Nothing was rescaled to force it.

degrades.to: the static trajectory, the three markers, both routes and every arrow
degrades.note: honours prefers-reduced-motion; with motion off no claim is lost.

svg.text: THE UNIVERSE OF BYTES AS A TORUS — S¹ × S¹
the FREQUENCY circle (position in the walk, ℤ/N — the ring buffer) × the AMPLITUDE circle (the byte, ℤ/256 — and it WRAPS) · the HOLE is ∅ and is not on the surface
⛔ HELD — checked against hatter FOUNDATION @ 1d9ea2cc on 2026-08-24. This figure DREW ON AN OPEN QUESTION (Q1) and REDREW CITED FACTORS. See FOUNDATION CHECK, foot of page.
Nothing is withdrawn. The claims are RE-STATUSED, the second circle is marked READING A rather than settled, and one pinned defect has been removed from the drawing.
THE TORUS — a perspective sketch. It NAMES the two circles; it does not measure them.
cat-byte.rzk: “C = ℤ/N : a ring buffer (positions, cyclic succ)” is the base · “objects = byte values {0..255}” is the fiber
Byte({ }) — the IDENTITY OBJECT, the monoidal unit I
unit law Byte({ }) ⊗ Byte(0) = Byte(0) — CITED, not redrawn: cat-byte.rzk §1.6 · FOUR-CATS.md §2
⛔ IsZeroNumber is NOT this test, and was drawn here until 2026-08-24. It cannot tell ABSENT from PRESENT-AND-ZERO. PINNED DEFECT — removed.
∅ — GENESIS, the 0 point. NOT a point of the surface: a HOLE HAS NO COORDINATES.
the SEQUENCE of bytes we are walking
⛔ READING A — foundation.md Q1 IS OPEN
ℤ/256 — the byte at that position
far half = hidden by the tube
A STEP IS A MOVE, NEVER A LOOKUP.
One step advances ±1 on the FREQUENCY circle and displaces by Δ on the AMPLITUDE circle.
“…we move from 63 to 61 — we DON’T go look up 61, we simply GO THERE.”
30 bytes · 19 distinct · range 0x20…0x74. Measured, not taken on report.
THE MOVES WORTH SEEING — a walk is a DISPLACEMENT, not a scan
⚠ THE WORD-BOUNDARY OBSERVATION IS CHART-DEPENDENT — so it is ILLUSTRATED, not asserted
Ran the control in cp037 (EBCDIC), the τ-leg map foundation.md §4b.2 keeps for exactly this:
✔ SURVIVES — the space is the MINIMUM byte in BOTH charts (0x20 ascii · 0x40 cp037),
so the two DIPS are real under both. That is what the square draws.
✘ FAILS — “the two deepest STEPS are the word boundaries” is TRUE in ascii (−69, −78)
and FALSE in cp037, where ‘M’→‘a’ (−83), which is INSIDE a word, beats ‘e’→‘␣’ (−69).
✘ And the BANDS INVERT: ascii puts lower ABOVE upper (97–116 vs 67–77); cp037 puts
lower BELOW upper (129–163 vs 195–212). Same word, same walk, different geometry.
⇒ These are facts about the CHART, never about walks. Declared under illustrates.
⛔ AND THE FULL WALK WILL NOT FIT ON THE TORUS — measured, not eyeballed
A perspective torus at 38° shows only the band of the amplitude circle visible at EVERY
longitude: ψ ∈ 54°…126° — 72° of 360°, i.e. 51 byte values, 20% of the circle.
This string spans 84 values (118°) and DOES NOT FIT; “Composable” spans 48 (68°) and does.
⇒ So the torus carries the first WORD, and the square carries all 30. The square is not a
convenience — at this projection it is the only UNDISTORTED view of the walk.
Nothing is compressed to make it fit. A rescaled amplitude axis would be a lie about ℤ/256.
THE FUNDAMENTAL SQUARE — the torus UNROLLED. All 30 positions. This is where the geometry is exact and nothing is hidden.
BOTH pairs of opposite edges identified · vertical seam 256 ≡ 0 is FORCED · horizontal seam is READING A of the OPEN Q1 · 0x6f + 254 = 0x16d ≡ 0x6d (mod 256)
top edge ≡ bottom edge — the SEAM is 256 ≡ 0 (FORCED on either reading of Q1)
left ≡ right — position N−1 NEXT-to 0 · READING A, Q1 OPEN
Δ = +254 — the SAME move, the long way round
it does not stop at 255; it wraps
the two ␣ are the DEEPEST points — word boundaries, visible as displacement
(true under ascii AND cp037; the deepest-STEP reading is not — see the panel above)
FREQUENCY — the SEQUENCE of bytes we are walking (position) · READING A of the OPEN Q1
AMPLITUDE — the BYTE at that position (0…255) · ℤ/256, FORCED

PATH A = PATH B
The displacement is a faithful MOVE. Nothing is fetched, and nothing is looked up.
THE LAW — what must hold for this to be a torus
The universe is the PRODUCT of two circles. The base is
ℤ/N, a ring buffer with cyclic successor — the FREQUENCY
circle. The fiber is the byte, 0…255, cyclic under NEXT —
the AMPLITUDE circle. A point IS the pair.
A step is a DISPLACEMENT on both circles at once. ∅ has
no pair, so ∅ is the hole and not a point of the surface.
If this fails, the figure is a picture of two circles, not a torus.
⛔ Naming the base “the ring buffer” is READING A — Q1 is OPEN.
The AMPLITUDE half is FORCED on either reading; this half is not.
THE CLAIMS — asserted, versus merely illustrated
ASSERTED — declared in <metadata>, all four UNPROVEN:
· c-torus-pi1 / c-torus-pi2 — a point IS the pair
· c-go-there — b = a + (b − a): a displacement is a MOVE
· c-wrap — Δ = −2 and Δ = +254 are the SAME MOVE (‘o’→‘m’)
· a-genesis — ∅ is LEFT by one genesis fold (an arrow, no square)
ILLUSTRATED — drawn, and NOT asserted:
· the perspective torus — a sketch, not a measurement
· everything the MOTION adds, and both word-boundary readings
Compass rules on the block. Stencil emits it and does not judge it.
An unmarked claim is an assertion that cannot fail; there are none here.
WHAT THIS DIAGRAM CANNOT SHOW
· Where byte 0 sits on the amplitude circle is a DRAWING
CONVENTION. Nothing here fixes the meridian’s origin.
· N is NOT ruled — and the register’s numbers are NOT
candidates: cat-bytes.md §3c — “the register is the
MEASUREMENT of ∫A, NOT the base category.” Corrected.
· cat-byte’s morphisms are ADJACENCY (byte-pair edges) and
are register-OBSERVED DATA — NOT ±1 on either circle.
· The fiber of ∫A is B-elt = Fin 256 + the unit I. Only the
Fin 256 part is ON the surface; I is the hole.
· The register is not drawn. [[SUBSTRATE-CANON]]
WHAT THE MOTION ASSERTS — motion can smuggle a claim, so it is DECLARED
· c-wrap — two heads leave ‘o’ 0x6f TOGETHER, one stepping −2 and one +254
through the seam. They ARRIVE TOGETHER at ‘m’ 0x6d. That CONVERGENCE is the assertion:
on a circle those are the same move. Status UNPROVEN, like the other three.
· a-genesis — the head LEAVES the hole. ∅ → the surface is one genesis fold.
WHAT IT ONLY ILLUSTRATES — no claim is made by any of these
· the swept CURVE of the genesis glide. The FOLD is one step, not a path.
· the GLIDE between marked positions. The frequency circle is ℤ/N and DISCRETE —
gliding asserts nothing about anything lying between position 0 and position 1.
· one full turn back to position 0 — the cyclic successor. N is still not ruled.
· the word-boundary DIPS and the three BANDS — chart facts, not walk facts. Controlled.

ANTENNA TIER: declarative SMIL on the VIEWER’S clock — no frame sequence, no wall-clock at authoring time. Honours prefers-reduced-motion; with motion off the static trajectory, markers, routes and arrows carry every claim.
FOUNDATION CHECK — /git/thecowboyai/hatter @ 1d9ea2cc, sources read 2026-08-24 · VERDICT: (c) THEY DISAGREE, and (a) IT REDRAWS. Both — and (c) outranks.
⛔ DISAGREEMENT 1 — Q1 IS OPEN AND THIS FIGURE ANSWERED IT SILENTLY.
foundation.md §4.2 / §9 Q1: is the second circle POSITION-WITHIN-A-SEQUENCE (A), or does
“which byte in which sequence” make the SEQUENCE a coordinate (B)? Foundation: “I am not
choosing … A ruling is owed BEFORE anything is drawn on it.” This figure drew READING A and
asserted it. The left≡right FREQUENCY seam IS that commitment. The amplitude seam is NOT.
⛔ DISAGREEMENT 2 — IsZeroNumber WAS DRAWN AS THE ∅-TEST. It is a PINNED DEFECT.
“ZeroNumber implies Byte(0) not Byte({ })” — it cannot tell ABSENT from PRESENT-AND-ZERO,
and a hole has NO COORDINATES to detect. Removed; Byte({ }) is the unit I.
[pin: feedback_byte_empty_is_the_hole_not_byte_zero]. My label “an empty byte sequence” was
wrong the same way: it is a BYTE whose CONTENT is absent, not a missing byte.
(a) REDRAWN — already asserted elsewhere, so now CITED and not claimed here:
· the floor is T² = S¹ × S¹ · Byte({ }) is the HOLE and IS I ..... foundation.md §4.1
· S¹value = ℤ/256, exactly 256 pts · PREV/NEXT ARE adjacency ... §4.2, both FORCED
· GO THERE, not lookup (Modulate / Demodulate) ................. cat-bytes.md §0.1
· A-fiber is CONSTANT ⇒ the bundle IS trivial ⇒ torus, not Klein cat-bytes.md §3d
⇒ so my “trivial vs Klein bottle, untested” caveat was UNDER-claiming. Discharged.
(b) GENUINELY NEW — the FUNDAMENTAL SQUARE and c-wrap. Neither document draws either,
and c-wrap rides only on the VALUE circle, which is FORCED on either reading of Q1.
⚠ ALSO FOUND, AND NOT MINE TO RESOLVE — §4.2 lists T² as FORCED “on either reading”,
then says reading B makes the floor “not T²”. Reported to Compass, not adjusted.
the FREQUENCY circle — READING A of the OPEN Q1: position in the walk, ℤ/N.
the AMPLITUDE circle — the byte, ℤ/256. It wraps.
a WALK — a displacement, never a lookup.

Arrowheads are DELIBERATE: every arrow is an olog ASPECT with a domain and a codomain. ⚠ NOT all are Cat(byte) morphisms — Cat(byte)’s are register-OBSERVED adjacency (B-le); a-short / a-long are this olog’s.
